title.zh: 卷399 列傳一百八十六 吕贤基 邹鸣鹤 戴熙 汤贻汾 张芾 黄琮 陶廷杰 冯培元 孙铭恩 沈炳垣 张锡庚
title.en: Volume 399 Biographies 186: Lv Xianji, Zou Minghe, Dai Xi, Tang Yifen, Zhang Fei, Huang Cong, Tao Tingjie, Feng Peiyuan, Sun Mingen, Shen Bingyuan, Zhang Xigeng
title.raw: 卷399 列傳一百八十六 吕贤基 邹鸣鹤 戴熙 汤贻汾 张芾 黄琮 陶廷杰 冯培元 孙铭恩 沈炳垣 张锡庚

sentences.zh: 呂賢基，字鶴田，安徽旌德人。

translations.literal: Lü Xianji, styled Hetian, was a native of Jingde in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Xianji, styled Hetian, was from Jingde in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the fifteenth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷御史、給事中，持正敢言，數論時政得失，多所採用。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor and supervising secretary, upheld integrity and spoke boldly, repeatedly discussing the gains and losses of current policy, and many of his proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to censor and supervising secretary, where he stood on principle and spoke out freely, repeatedly memorializing on the strengths and failings of government policy; many of his recommendations were taken up.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，應詔上封事，請懋聖學，正人心，育人才，恤民隱，尤被嘉納。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne, in response to an edict he submitted a sealed memorial requesting vigorous imperial learning, rectification of the human heart, cultivation of talent, and relief of the people's hidden grievances, and it was especially praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, he responded to the imperial call for memorials with a sealed submission urging stronger royal study, moral renewal, the nurturing of talent, and attention to the people's hidden hardships; it was especially well received.

sentences.zh: 遷鴻臚寺卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，超擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was exceptionally promoted to vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted ahead of schedule to vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 二年，以時事可危，疏請下詔求言，略曰：「粵西會匪滋事，二年以來，命將出師，尚無成效，甚至圍攻省城，大肆猖獗。

translations.literal: In the second year, because current affairs were perilous, he memorialized requesting an edict calling for candid advice, saying in summary: 'The secret-society bandits in western Guangdong have risen in revolt; for two years generals have been dispatched on campaign without notable success, and the rebels have even besieged the provincial capital and run rampant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, seeing the times turning dangerous, he memorialized asking the throne to issue an edict inviting open counsel. He wrote in part: 'Secret-society rebels in western Guangdong have been in turmoil for two years. Generals have been sent against them, yet there has been little success; the rebels have even besieged the provincial capital and grown wildly bold.

sentences.zh: 南河豐工未能合龍，重運阻滯，災民屯聚，在在堪虞。

translations.literal: The Feng works on the South River have failed to close the breach, grain transport on the Grand Canal is blocked, disaster victims are massed everywhere, and at every point there is cause for alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The Feng River works on the South River have still not been closed, heavy grain transport is stalled, disaster victims are gathering everywhere, and danger threatens on every side.

sentences.zh: 河工費五百萬，軍需費一千馀萬，部臣束手無措，必致掊克朘削，邦本愈搖。

translations.literal: River works will cost five million taels and military supplies more than ten million; the ministers of the Board are helpless, which will inevitably lead to squeezing and stripping the people, and the foundation of the state will be shaken all the more.
translations.idiomatic: River works will cost five million taels and military supplies more than ten million. The board ministers are at their wits' end, and the result will surely be extortion and ruinous levies that further undermine the state's foundations.

sentences.zh: 今日事勢，譬之於病，元氣血脈，枯竭已甚，外邪又熾，若再諱疾忌醫，愈難為救。

translations.literal: Today's situation may be compared to illness: the vital energy and blood are already greatly exhausted, while external evils blaze anew; if we again conceal the disease and shun the physician, rescue will become all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: The present situation is like a grave illness: the body's vital strength is already badly depleted, and external afflictions are raging again. If the court once more hides the sickness and refuses the doctor, recovery will become nearly impossible.

sentences.zh: 惟有開通喉舌，廣覓良方，庶可補救萬一。

translations.literal: Only by opening the throat and tongue and widely seeking effective remedies can we hope to remedy matters even in the slightest degree.
translations.idiomatic: Only by giving voice to candid counsel and searching broadly for sound remedies can we hope to salvage even a fraction of what remains.

sentences.zh: 請特旨令大小臣工悉去忌諱，一改洩沓之故習，各抒所見，以期集思廣益。」

translations.literal: I request a special edict ordering officials great and small to cast off all taboos, altogether change the old habit of slack evasion, each express his views, and thereby gather wisdom for broad benefit.'
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a special edict command officials at every level to drop their inhibitions, break with the old habit of evasive delay, and speak their minds freely so that many minds may strengthen policy.'

sentences.zh: 疏入，諭部院大臣、九卿、科道有言責者，各據見聞，直言無隱。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict instructed the ministers of boards and provinces, the Nine Chief Ministers, and the censorial officials charged with remonstrance to speak frankly according to what each had seen and heard, without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the throne ordered ministers of boards and provinces, the Nine Chief Ministers, and remonstrating censorial officials to report frankly on what they had witnessed, withholding nothing.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，命賢基馳赴安徽會同巡撫蔣文慶及週天爵辦理防剿事宜，賢基疏言：「江寧以東西梁山為要隘，必先扼守。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he was ordered to hurry to Anhui to join Governor Jiang Wenqing and Zhou Tianjue in handling defense and suppression affairs. Xianji memorialized, saying: 'Jiangning's vital passes are the eastern and western Liang Mountains, and these must first be held firmly.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Xianji was ordered to rush to Anhui to work with Governor Jiang Wenqing and Zhou Tianjue on defense and suppression. He memorialized: 'The eastern and western Liang Mountains are the key passes of Jiangning and must be seized and held first.

sentences.zh: 廬州為江淮門戶，宜令重臣駐★。

translations.literal: Luzhou is the gateway between the Yangzi and Huai regions; a senior official should be stationed there to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou is the gateway of the Jianghuai region, and a senior official ought to be posted there to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 巢湖出江當梁山上游，地方匪徒宜招撫，免為賊用，且可與梁山為犄角。」

translations.literal: Chaohu Lake debouches into the river upstream of the Liang Mountains; local bandits there should be pacified by inducement so they are not used by the rebels, and they can moreover form a pincer with the Liang Mountains.'
translations.idiomatic: Chaohu Lake flows into the Yangzi above the Liang Mountains. Local bandits there should be won over so they are not turned to rebel use, and they can then support the Liang positions in a pincer.'

sentences.zh: 上嘉納，不及施行，而安慶、江寧先後陷。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this, but before it could be carried out, Anqing and Jiangning fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan, but before it could be put into effect Anqing and Jiangning had already fallen in turn.

sentences.zh: 奏調給事中袁甲三、知府趙畇幫辦團練防剿，又調編修李鴻章等襄軍事。

translations.literal: He memorialized to transfer supervising secretary Yuan Jiasan and prefect Zhao Yun to assist in organizing militia for defense and suppression, and also transferred compiler Li Hongzhang and others to help with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He requested the transfer of supervising secretary Yuan Jiasan and prefect Zhao Yun to help organize militia for defense and suppression, and also brought in compiler Li Hongzhang and others to assist with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 偕週天爵疏言：「事當分任。

translations.literal: Together with Zhou Tianjue he memorialized, saying: 'Affairs should be divided by responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Zhou Tianjue he submitted a memorial saying: 'These tasks should be divided by responsibility.

sentences.zh: 團練專令殲除土匪；

translations.literal: The militia should be charged solely with exterminating local bandits;
translations.idiomatic: Militia forces should be assigned exclusively to wiping out local bandits;

sentences.zh: 牧令守本境，統帥勦賊，不得遠駐百里之外，以免推諉。」

translations.literal: magistrates should defend their own jurisdictions, and commanders should suppress rebels without encamping a hundred li away, so as to avoid shifting blame.'
translations.idiomatic: local magistrates should hold their own districts, and field commanders should pursue rebels without posting themselves a hundred li away, so that no one can pass the blame.'

sentences.zh: 上韙之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor endorsed the proposal.

sentences.zh: 安徽境內無大枝勁旅，團練亦散漫無可恃。

translations.literal: Within Anhui there were no large, strong regular forces, and the militia were also scattered and unreliable.
translations.idiomatic: Anhui had no large regular forces of any strength, and the militia were scattered and could not be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 七月，湖北敗賊竄陷英山，擾太湖，分犯洪家埠，賢基檄游擊賡音太、伍登庸擊走之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, defeated rebels from Hubei fled in and seized Yingshan, harassed Taihu, and sent detachments to attack Hongjiabu. Xianji dispatched battalion commanders Geng Yintai and Wu Dengyong, who drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month defeated rebels from Hubei broke into Yingshan, raided Taihu, and sent detachments against Hongjiabu. Xianji ordered battalion commanders Geng Yintai and Wu Dengyong to beat them back.

sentences.zh: 八月，賊復自江西竄踞安慶，賢基赴舒城、桐城勸募團練，為官軍聲援。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the rebels again fled from Jiangxi and seized Anqing. Xianji went to Shucheng and Tongcheng to encourage and recruit militia as a supporting force for the regular army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the rebels again swept in from Jiangxi and occupied Anqing. Xianji went to Shucheng and Tongcheng to raise militia and give the regular forces a supporting presence.

sentences.zh: 賡音太、伍登庸戰歿於集賢關。

translations.literal: Geng Yintai and Wu Dengyong died in battle at Jixian Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Yintai and Wu Dengyong were killed in battle at Jixian Pass.

sentences.zh: 賊犯桐城，紳士馬三俊率練勇迎戰失利，遂失守。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked Tongcheng; the gentry leader Ma Sanjun led militia to meet them in battle but was defeated, and the city was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels struck Tongcheng, gentry leader Ma Sanjun led militia out to fight but was beaten, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 已革按察使張熙宇退駐大關，賢基抗疏劾之。

translations.literal: The dismissed provincial judge Zhang Xiyu had withdrawn and encamped at Daguan. Xianji submitted a forceful memorial impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: The dismissed provincial judge Zhang Xiyu had pulled back and encamped at Daguan, and Xianji submitted a strong memorial impeaching him.

sentences.zh: 時方駐舒城，或告以無守土責，未轄一兵，賊鋒甚銳，可退守以圖再舉。

translations.literal: At the time he was stationed at Shucheng, and some advised him that he bore no territorial defense duty, commanded not a single soldier, and faced very sharp rebel pressure, and that he could withdraw to defend elsewhere and plan a fresh effort.
translations.idiomatic: He was then at Shucheng, and some urged that he had no duty to hold territory, commanded no troops of his own, and faced a very sharp rebel advance; he could withdraw and regroup for another attempt.

sentences.zh: 賢基曰：「奉命治鄉兵殺賊，當以死報國。

translations.literal: Xianji said: 'I was ordered to organize local militia and kill rebels; I should repay the state with my death.
translations.idiomatic: Xianji said: 'I was ordered to raise local militia and fight the rebels. I ought to repay the state with my life.

sentences.zh: 敢避寇倖免乎？」

translations.literal: How dare I flee the bandits and hope to escape alive?'
translations.idiomatic: How could I flee the enemy and hope to survive?'

sentences.zh: 十月賊至，登陴守禦，城陷，死之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the rebels arrived; he mounted the walls to defend, the city fell, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the rebels arrived. He took the walls to defend the city; when it fell, he died.

sentences.zh: 文宗初聞舒城失守，即曰：「賢基素懷忠義，必能大節無虧。」

translations.literal: When Wenzong first heard that Shucheng had fallen, he said at once: 'Xianji has always cherished loyalty and righteousness; he is sure to have preserved his great integrity unblemished.'
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong first heard that Shucheng had fallen, he said at once: 'Xianji has always been loyal and upright; he is sure to have kept his honor intact.'

sentences.zh: 及奏上，深悼惜之，贈尚書銜，加恩於舒城建專祠，擢其子編修錦文以侍讀用，賜銀三千兩，命錦文即日回籍治喪。

translations.literal: When the report was submitted, he deeply mourned and regretted the loss, posthumously granted the rank of minister, added favor by building a special shrine for him at Shucheng, promoted his son, compiler Jinwen, for appointment as reader-in-waiting, granted three thousand taels of silver, and ordered Jinwen to return home that same day to manage the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When the report arrived, the emperor deeply mourned him, posthumously granted him ministerial rank, ordered a special shrine built for him at Shucheng, promoted his son Jinwen, a compiler, for appointment as reader-in-waiting, granted three thousand taels of silver, and ordered Jinwen to return home at once to conduct the funeral.

sentences.zh: 予騎都尉世職，祀京師及本籍府城昭忠祠。

translations.literal: He was granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry and enshrined in the Hall of Loyalty and Devotion in the capital and in the prefectural city of his native place.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry and enshrined in the Hall of Loyalty and Devotion in the capital and in his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後安徽請祀鄉賢，特諭：「賢基品行端正，居官忠直，名副其實。」

translations.literal: Later Anhui requested that he be enshrined among local worthies, and a special edict stated: 'Xianji's character and conduct were upright, and in office he was loyal and straight; the title matches the reality.'
translations.idiomatic: Later Anhui asked that he be enshrined among local worthies, and a special edict declared: 'Xianji's character was upright and his official conduct loyal and direct; the honor is fully deserved.'

sentences.zh: 即報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted at once.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved immediately.

sentences.zh: 鄒鳴鶴，字鍾泉，江蘇無錫人。

translations.literal: Zou Minghe, styled Zhongquan, was a native of Wuxi in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Minghe, styled Zhongquan, was from Wuxi in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光二年進士，雲南即用知縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed magistrate directly to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the second year of Daoguang and was sent directly to Yunnan as a magistrate.

sentences.zh: 親老告近，改發河南，署新鄭，補羅山，有惠政。

translations.literal: Because his parents were elderly he requested a nearby posting, was reassigned to Henan, served as acting magistrate of Xinzheng, was appointed to Luoshan, and governed with benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents grew old he asked to serve nearer home, was reassigned to Henan, acted as magistrate of Xinzheng, then took permanent appointment at Luoshan, where his rule won popular goodwill.

sentences.zh: 母喪，去官。

translations.literal: When his mother died he left office.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he left office.

sentences.zh: 巡撫程祖洛疏陳鳴鶴政績，羅山紳民籥請保留河南，特旨允俟服闋以南、汝、陳、光四府州所屬酌補選缺，異數也。

translations.literal: Governor Cheng Zuluo memorialized Minghe's administrative achievements; the gentry and people of Luoshan petitioned to retain him in Henan, and a special edict permitted that after mourning he be assigned at discretion to vacancies under the four prefectures of Nan, Ru, Chen, and Guang—an exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Cheng Zuluo memorialized Minghe's record in office, and Luoshan's gentry and people petitioned to keep him in Henan. A special edict allowed that after mourning he might be assigned at discretion to vacancies in the Nan, Ru, Chen, and Guang prefectures—an exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 尋補光山，調祥符，擢蘭儀廳河工同知，護開歸陳許道。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed to Guangshan, transferred to Xiangfu, promoted to sub-prefect of river works at the Lanyi Office, and acted as intendant of the Kai-Gui-Chen-Xu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed to Guangshan, transferred to Xiangfu, promoted to sub-prefect of river works at the Lanyi Office, and served as acting intendant of the Kai-Gui-Chen-Xu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 以治河勞，晉秩知府。

translations.literal: For his labors in river control he was promoted in rank to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: For his work on river control he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 歷衛輝、陳州、開封。

translations.literal: He served successively at Weihui, Chenzhou, and Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession at Weihui, Chenzhou, and Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，河決祥符，水圍省城，鳴鶴露宿城上，盡力堵禦。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the river breached at Xiangfu, water surrounded the provincial capital, and Minghe slept in the open on the city wall, doing all he could to block and defend.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the river broke at Xiangfu and water encircled the provincial capital. Minghe slept on the walls and did everything he could to hold the breach.

sentences.zh: 有議遷省城於洛陽者，鳴鶴上議有六不可。

translations.literal: Some proposed moving the provincial capital to Luoyang; Minghe submitted a memorial setting forth six reasons why this should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed moving the provincial capital to Luoyang, Minghe submitted a memorial listing six reasons why that should not be done.

sentences.zh: 欽差大臣王鼎等據以疏陳，乃決議堅守。

translations.literal: The imperial commissioner Wang Ding and others memorialized on this basis, and the decision was made to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial commissioner Wang Ding and others memorialized accordingly, and the court resolved to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 凡曆七十馀日，水退城安。

translations.literal: Altogether more than seventy days passed before the water receded and the city was secure.
translations.idiomatic: After more than seventy days the waters fell and the city was saved.

sentences.zh: 論功，晉秩道員。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed he was promoted in rank to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，河決中牟，褫職留工，工竣，復原官，仍在工效力。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the river breached at Zhongmou; he was stripped of office but kept on the works, and when the project was completed his original rank was restored and he continued to serve on the project.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year the river broke at Zhongmou. He was dismissed from office but kept on the works; when the project was finished his rank was restored and he remained on the job.

sentences.zh: 丁生母憂，服闋，署彰衛懷道，尋授江西督糧道。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his birth mother; when mourning ended he acted as intendant of the Zhang-Wei-Huai Circuit, and soon afterward was appointed grain transport commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his birth mother he acted as intendant of the Zhang-Wei-Huai Circuit, then was appointed grain transport commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，詔舉賢才，戶部侍郎侯桐、兩江總督陸建瀛交章以鳴鶴薦，擢順天府尹。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne, an edict called for worthy talent; Vice Minister of Revenue Hou Tong and Governor-General Lu Jianying jointly recommended Minghe, and he was promoted to metropolitan prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, an edict called for men of talent. Vice Minister Hou Tong and Governor-General Lu Jianying jointly recommended Minghe, and he was promoted to metropolitan prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，擢廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted to governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted to governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 匪亂方熾，大學士賽尚阿督軍事，鳴鶴課吏治，治團練，撫卹被兵災民。

translations.literal: Bandit turmoil was then blazing; Grand Secretary Saishanga directed military affairs, while Minghe enforced official discipline, organized militia, and relieved people afflicted by war.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel turmoil was at its height. Grand Secretary Saishanga directed military affairs while Minghe tightened administration, organized militia, and relieved people suffering from the fighting.

sentences.zh: 二年，賊由永安突犯桂林，城中兵僅千人，倉猝防禦，提督向榮馳援，民心始定。

translations.literal: In the second year the rebels suddenly attacked Guilin from Yong'an; the city had only a thousand troops, and defense was hurriedly organized. Regional commander Xiang Rong rushed to aid, and public morale finally settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the rebels burst out of Yong'an and struck Guilin. The city had barely a thousand troops and had to organize defense in haste. Regional commander Xiang Rong raced to the rescue, and the people's panic eased.

sentences.zh: 總兵秦定三等續至，鳴鶴以諸軍無所統屬，自請督戰。

translations.literal: Brigade commanders Qin Dingsan and others arrived in succession; Minghe, seeing that the various armies had no unified command, volunteered to direct the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade commanders including Qin Dingsan arrived in turn. Seeing that the various forces had no unified command, Minghe volunteered to direct the fighting himself.

sentences.zh: 分遣諸將擊賊，相持月馀，賊百計攻城，屢卻。

translations.literal: He dispatched the generals to strike the rebels; the two sides faced each other for more than a month, and though the rebels tried every means to storm the city, they were repeatedly repulsed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his generals out against the rebels. The two sides remained locked for more than a month, and though the rebels tried every stratagem to take the city, they were driven back again and again.

sentences.zh: 賊遂分竄，賽尚阿促向榮追擊，鳴鶴堅留防賊回竄，互疏爭。

translations.literal: The rebels then split and fled; Saishanga urged Xiang Rong to pursue, while Minghe insisted on staying to guard against their return, and the two exchanged conflicting memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then split and fled. Saishanga pressed Xiang Rong to pursue, while Minghe insisted on staying to guard against their return, and the two exchanged opposing memorials.

sentences.zh: 賊尋陷興安、全州，入湖南，詔褫鳴鶴職，以守城功免治罪。

translations.literal: The rebels soon seized Xing'an and Quanzhou and entered Hunan; an edict stripped Minghe of office but exempted him from punishment because of his merit in defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon took Xing'an and Quanzhou and entered Hunan. An edict removed Minghe from office but spared him punishment because of his service in defending Guilin.

sentences.zh: 洎回籍，賊已陷武昌。

translations.literal: By the time he returned home, the rebels had already taken Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he returned home, the rebels had already captured Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，陸建瀛赴九江督師，疏請起鳴鶴籌辦沿江防務。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Lu Jianying went to Jiujiang to direct the army and memorialized requesting that Minghe be recalled to organize defenses along the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Lu Jianying went to Jiujiang to direct the army and memorialized asking that Minghe be recalled to organize defenses along the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 已病，或沮其行。

translations.literal: He was already ill, and some tried to dissuade him from going.
translations.idiomatic: He was already ill, and some tried to dissuade him from going.

sentences.zh: 曰：「此吾補過報國之日也！」

translations.literal: He said: 'This is the day for me to atone and repay the state!'
translations.idiomatic: He said: 'This is my day to atone and serve the state!'

sentences.zh: 建瀛旋退江寧，獲罪，命鳴鶴與將軍祥厚等籌商守禦。

translations.literal: Lu Jianying soon withdrew to Jiangning and was punished; Minghe was ordered, together with General Xianghou and others, to consult on defense.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jianying soon fell back to Jiangning and was punished. Minghe was ordered to join General Xianghou and others in planning the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 建瀛見其病甚，欲為奏請還家養疴，鳴鶴不可。

translations.literal: Lu Jianying saw how seriously ill he was and wanted to memorialize asking that he be sent home to recover, but Minghe would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jianying saw how gravely ill he was and wanted to memorialize asking that he be sent home to recover, but Minghe refused.

sentences.zh: 及江寧陷，書絕命詞曰：「臣力難圖報稱，臣心仰答九重。

translations.literal: When Jiangning fell he wrote a final testament, saying: 'Your servant's strength cannot achieve repayment, but your servant's heart looks up to answer the Ninefold Heights.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangning fell he wrote a final testament: 'My strength cannot repay what I owe, but my heart still rises to answer the throne.

sentences.zh: 三次守城盡節，庶幾全始全終。」

translations.literal: Having thrice defended cities to the utmost integrity, I may perhaps finish as I began.'
translations.idiomatic: Having defended three cities to the death, I may at least finish as I began.'

sentences.zh: 遣人持付其子，自率隊出，至三山街，賊見識之，曰：「此守桂林之鄒巡撫也！」

translations.literal: He sent someone to deliver it to his son, then led a detachment out himself. At Sanshan Street the rebels recognized him and said: 'This is Governor Zou who defended Guilin!'
translations.idiomatic: He sent the note to his son by messenger, then led a detachment out himself. At Sanshan Street the rebels recognized him and cried: 'This is Governor Zou who held Guilin!'

sentences.zh: 呼其名詬之。

translations.literal: They called his name and reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: They shouted his name and cursed him.

sentences.zh: 鳴鶴亦罵不絕口，被支解而死。

translations.literal: Minghe also cursed without cease and was dismembered to death.
translations.idiomatic: Minghe cursed them without pause and was hacked to pieces.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈道銜，賜卹。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted circuit rank and given condolence honors.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously granted circuit rank and given mourning honors.

sentences.zh: 同治初，江南既平，曾國籓疏陳鳴鶴生平政績及殉節狀，請加恩優恤。

translations.literal: In the early Tongzhi reign, after Jiangnan had been pacified, Zeng Guofan memorialized Minghe's lifetime administrative achievements and the circumstances of his martyrdom, requesting additional favor and generous condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign, after Jiangnan had been pacified, Zeng Guofan memorialized Minghe's career and the circumstances of his death, asking for additional honors.

sentences.zh: 御史硃震言鳴鶴匿民居遇害，非臨陣捐軀者比，請罷之。

translations.literal: Censor Zhu Zhen said Minghe had hidden in a private house when killed and was not comparable to one who gave his life on the battlefield, and requested that the honors be revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhu Zhen argued that Minghe had been killed while hiding in a private house and was not comparable to a man who died fighting in the field, and asked that the honors be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 編修硃福基等復以鳴鶴被難聞見各殊，呈請下兩江總督馬新貽確查。

translations.literal: Compiler Zhu Fuji and others, noting that accounts of Minghe's death differed, submitted a request that Governor-General Ma Xinyi of the Two Jiangs conduct a thorough investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Zhu Fuji and others, noting that reports of Minghe's death conflicted, asked that Governor-General Ma Xinyi of the Two Jiangs investigate.

sentences.zh: 新貽覆奏紳耆咸稱鳴鶴協同防守，誓以身殉，罵賊被戕，無避匿民居之事。

translations.literal: Ma Xinyi reported back that gentry elders all said Minghe had joined in the defense, sworn to die for the cause, cursed the rebels and been killed, and that there was no matter of hiding in a private house.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xinyi reported back that local gentry all testified that Minghe had joined the defense, sworn to die for the city, cursed the rebels, and been killed in the fighting, with no question of hiding in a private house.

sentences.zh: 詔依巡撫例議卹，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡壯節。

translations.literal: An edict ordered condolence according to the precedent for governors, granted the combined hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, and conferred the posthumous title Zhuangjie.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered mourning honors according to the precedent for governors, granted the combined hereditary ranks of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, and gave him the posthumous title Zhuangjie, 'Steadfast in Integrity.'

sentences.zh: 後祀河南名宦祠。

translations.literal: Later he was enshrined in the Hall of Eminent Officials of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later enshrined in Henan's Hall of Eminent Officials.

sentences.zh: 戴熙，字醇士，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Dai Xi, styled Chunshi, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Xi, styled Chunshi, was from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the twelfth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 大考二等，擢贊善，遷中允。

translations.literal: In the triennial examination he ranked second class, was promoted to reader, and transferred to assistant director of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the triennial examination he placed second class, was promoted to reader, and then transferred to assistant director of the Academy.

sentences.zh: 十八年，入直南書房。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he entered attendance in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he entered service in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 督廣東學政，任滿，請終養。

translations.literal: He supervised education in Guangdong; when his term ended he requested leave to care for his parents until their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: He served as educational commissioner of Guangdong, and when his term ended he asked leave to care for his parents at home.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，服闋，未補官，复督廣東學政，累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, when mourning ended, before receiving a new appointment he again supervised education in Guangdong and was promoted step by step to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, when mourning ended, he was again appointed educational commissioner of Guangdong before taking another post, and rose step by step to grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授兵部侍郎，仍直南書房。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed vice minister of War and continued attendance in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed vice minister of War while continuing service in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 先是，廣東因士民阻英人入城，相持者數年。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Guangdong the gentry and people had resisted the entry of the English into the city, and the standoff had lasted several years.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Guangdong the gentry and people had resisted British entry into the city, and the standoff had lasted several years.

sentences.zh: 至二十九年，英人懾於民怒，暫罷議。

translations.literal: By the twenty-ninth year the English, awed by popular anger, temporarily dropped the issue.
translations.idiomatic: By the twenty-ninth year the British, intimidated by public anger, temporarily dropped the issue.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘉悅，以為奇功，錫封總督徐廣縉子爵，巡撫葉名琛男爵。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was delighted, regarded it as a singular achievement, and ennobled Governor-General Xu Guangjin as marquis and Governor Ye Mingchen as baron.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was delighted, treated it as a singular achievement, and ennobled Governor-General Xu Guangjin as marquis and Governor Ye Mingchen as baron.

sentences.zh: 會熙召對，論及之。

translations.literal: When Xi was summoned for audience, the matter was discussed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi was summoned for audience, the matter came up.

sentences.zh: 熙言廣東民風素所諳悉，督撫所奏，恐涉鋪張，非可終恃，上不懌。

translations.literal: Xi said he was well acquainted with the customs of Guangdong and feared the governor-general's and governor's reports were exaggerated and could not be relied on forever; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said he knew Guangdong's local temperament well and feared the governor-general's and governor's reports were inflated and could not be relied on indefinitely. The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 尋命書扇，有帖體字，傳旨申飭。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to write a fan and used a character in the calligraphic style of rubbings; an edict was transmitted rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was ordered to inscribe a fan and used a character in the epigraphic style; an edict rebuking him followed.

sentences.zh: 越日，命南書房書扁額，內監傳諭指派同直張錫庚，戒勿交寫誤字之戴熙。

translations.literal: The next day, when the Southern Study was ordered to write a plaque, the eunuch transmitted instructions assigning his colleague on duty Zhang Xigeng and warning them not to give the task to Dai Xi, who wrote erroneous characters.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when the Southern Study was ordered to inscribe a plaque, a eunuch relayed instructions assigning Zhang Xigeng, who was on duty with him, and warning them not to give the work to Dai Xi, who had written mistaken characters.

sentences.zh: 未幾，罷其入直。

translations.literal: Before long he was removed from attendance duty.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was removed from Southern Study duty.

sentences.zh: 熙知眷衰，稱病請開缺，上益怒，降三品京堂休致。

translations.literal: Xi knew imperial favor had waned, pleaded illness and requested leave from office, the emperor grew still angrier, and he was reduced to third-rank metropolitan official and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Xi saw that imperial favor had faded, pleaded illness and asked to leave office, the emperor grew still angrier, and he was reduced to third-rank metropolitan official and retired.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，詔舉人才，尚書孫瑞珍以熙薦，召來京候簡用，因病未至。

translations.literal: In the early Xianfeng reign an edict called for talent; Minister Sun Ruizhen recommended Xi, who was summoned to the capital to await appointment but did not come because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign an edict called for men of talent. Minister Sun Ruizhen recommended Xi, who was summoned to the capital to await appointment but did not come because of illness.

sentences.zh: 粵匪踞江寧，浙江戒嚴。

translations.literal: Guangdong rebels occupied Jiangning and Zhejiang was placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong rebels held Jiangning, and Zhejiang was placed on alert.

sentences.zh: 熙偕官紳勸諭捐輸，舉行團練。

translations.literal: Xi joined officials and gentry in encouraging contributions and organizing militia.
translations.idiomatic: Xi worked with officials and gentry to encourage donations and organize militia.

sentences.zh: 八年，粵匪由江西擾浙東，熙助巡撫晏端書籌調兵食，乞援鄰境。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Guangdong rebels from Jiangxi harassed eastern Zhejiang; Xi assisted Governor Yan Duanshu in arranging troops and supplies and requested aid from neighboring jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Guangdong rebels from Jiangxi raided eastern Zhejiang. Xi helped Governor Yan Duanshu arrange troops and supplies and asked neighboring provinces for aid.

sentences.zh: 援師至，賊未得逞，漸退。

translations.literal: Relief troops arrived, the rebels failed to achieve their aim, and gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Relief troops arrived, the rebels failed to break through, and gradually withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以治團練勞，加二品頂戴。

translations.literal: For his labors in organizing militia he was granted the second-rank official's cap button.
translations.idiomatic: For his work organizing militia he was granted the second-rank official's cap button.

sentences.zh: 杭州初有民兵八百人，又選鋒數百，事緩，以資絀，減少半。

translations.literal: Hangzhou at first had eight hundred militia, and several hundred more were selected as vanguard troops; when affairs eased and funds were short, the force was cut by half.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou initially had eight hundred militiamen, with several hundred more chosen as shock troops; when the crisis eased and funds ran short, the force was cut in half.

sentences.zh: 十年，粵匪由安徽廣德入浙，連陷數縣，犯湖州、武康。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Guangdong rebels entered Zhejiang from Guangde in Anhui, seized several counties in succession, and threatened Huzhou and Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Guangdong rebels entered Zhejiang from Guangde in Anhui, took several counties in succession, and threatened Huzhou and Wukang.

sentences.zh: 熙以所部練勇付按察使段光清，會旗兵防獨松、千秋等關。

translations.literal: Xi entrusted the militia under his command to provincial judge Duan Guangqing and joined banner troops in defending the passes at Dusong, Qianqiu, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Xi placed his militia under provincial judge Duan Guangqing and joined banner troops in defending the passes at Dusong, Qianqiu, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 賊至，斂兵入城守。

translations.literal: When the rebels arrived, the troops were withdrawn into the city to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived, the troops were pulled back into the city to hold it.

sentences.zh: 熙謂用兵無獨守孤城之理，宜分營城外相犄角，又議乘賊初至迎擊，皆未行。

translations.literal: Xi said there was no principle in warfare of defending a lone city by itself; camps should be divided outside the walls in mutual support, and he also proposed striking the rebels as soon as they arrived, but none of this was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Xi argued that warfare did not permit defending a lone city in isolation; camps should be posted outside the walls in mutual support, and he also proposed meeting the rebels as soon as they arrived, but none of these plans was adopted.

sentences.zh: 熙與弟燾助守西北隅，砲斃黃衣賊一人，賊遽退匿山後。

translations.literal: Xi and his brother Tao helped defend the northwest corner; cannon fire killed one rebel in yellow garb, and the rebels at once withdrew and hid behind the hills.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and his brother Tao helped hold the northwest corner. Cannon fire killed one rebel in yellow garb, and the rebels quickly fell back behind the hills.

sentences.zh: 眾謂賊且遁，熙料其詐，偵之，果轉赴西南。

translations.literal: The crowd said the rebels were about to flee, but Xi suspected a ruse; when he sent scouts, they indeed turned toward the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: People thought the rebels were about to flee, but Xi suspected a feint; when he sent scouts, they found the rebels had turned toward the southwest.

sentences.zh: 晝夜環攻，久雨，兵疲。

translations.literal: Day and night the rebels besieged the city on all sides; prolonged rain exhausted the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels besieged the city day and night. Endless rain wore the defenders down.

sentences.zh: 賊於宋鎮湖門故址穴地轟城，遂陷，熙赴水死之。

translations.literal: The rebels tunneled under the old site of Songzhen Humen and blasted the wall; the city fell, and Xi entered the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tunneled under the old site of Songzhen Humen and blasted the wall. The city fell, and Xi drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 弟煦、媳金、及甥王朝榮，同殉。

translations.literal: His brother Xu, his daughter-in-law Jin, and his nephew Wang Chaorong died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Xu, his daughter-in-law Jin, and his nephew Wang Chaorong died with him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈尚書銜，建專祠，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡文節。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted ministerial rank, a special shrine was built, he was given the combined hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, and the posthumous title Wenjie was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously granted ministerial rank, given a special shrine, awarded the combined hereditary ranks of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, and given the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Cultured Integrity.'

sentences.zh: 弟煦，精算學，自有傳。

translations.literal: His brother Xu was expert in mathematics and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Xu was an expert in mathematics and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 熙雅尚絕俗，尤善畫。

translations.literal: Xi cultivated an austere, unconventional manner and was especially skilled at painting.
translations.idiomatic: Xi cultivated an austere, unconventional manner and was especially skilled at painting.

sentences.zh: 當視學廣東，陛辭，宣宗諭曰：「古人之作畫，須行萬里路。

translations.literal: When he was about to supervise education in Guangdong and took leave at court, Emperor Xuanzong instructed him, saying: 'In ancient times, to paint well one had to travel ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: When he was leaving court to supervise education in Guangdong, Emperor Xuanzong told him: 'In ancient times, to paint well one had to travel ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 此行遍歷山川，畫當益進。」

translations.literal: On this journey you will traverse mountains and rivers; your painting should improve all the more.'
translations.idiomatic: On this journey you will travel through mountains and rivers; your painting should improve all the more.'

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 後以直言黜。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed for speaking bluntly.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dismissed for speaking bluntly.

sentences.zh: 及殉節，遂益為世重。

translations.literal: When he died for his integrity, he came to be valued all the more by the world.
translations.idiomatic: When he died for his integrity, the world valued him all the more.

sentences.zh: 同時湯貽汾畫負盛名，與熙相匹。

translations.literal: At the same time Tang Yifen enjoyed great fame in painting and was Xi's equal.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Tang Yifen enjoyed great fame as a painter and was Xi's equal.

sentences.zh: 亦殉江寧之難，同以忠義顯，世稱戴、湯雲。

translations.literal: He too died in the Jiangning disaster; both became renowned for loyalty and righteousness, and the age called them Dai and Tang together.
translations.idiomatic: He too died in the fall of Jiangning; both became renowned for loyalty and righteousness, and the age spoke of them together as Dai and Tang.

sentences.zh: 貽汾，字雨生，江蘇武進人。

translations.literal: Yifen, styled Yusheng, was a native of Wujin in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Yifen, styled Yusheng, was from Wujin in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 祖大奎，官福建鳳山知縣，守城殉節，父荀業同死，見忠義傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dakui served as magistrate of Fengshan in Fujian, died defending the city in martyrdom, and his father Xunye died with him; see the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dakui had served as magistrate of Fengshan in Fujian and died defending the city; his father Xunye died with him. Their story appears in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 貽汾少有俊才。

translations.literal: Yifen showed outstanding talent from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Yifen showed outstanding talent from youth.

sentences.zh: 家貧，以難廕襲世職，授守備，累擢浙江樂清協副將。

translations.literal: His family was poor; because of the hardship of his forebears' deaths he inherited a hereditary office, was appointed garrison commander, and was promoted step by step to deputy regional commander of the Leqing garrison in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor. Because of his forebears' martyrdom he inherited a hereditary office, was appointed garrison commander, and rose step by step to deputy regional commander of the Leqing garrison in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 歷官治軍捕盜有聲。

translations.literal: In successive posts he won renown for governing troops and capturing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In successive posts he won renown for governing troops and capturing bandits.

sentences.zh: 尚氣節，工詩畫，政績文章為時重。

translations.literal: He valued integrity, was skilled in poetry and painting, and his administrative achievements and literary work were highly regarded in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He valued integrity, was skilled in poetry and painting, and his administrative record and literary work were highly regarded in his day.

sentences.zh: 晚辭官僑居江寧。

translations.literal: In his later years he resigned office and lived as a sojourner in Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he resigned office and lived in Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 及粵匪熾，貽汾見時事日亟，語人曰：「吾年七十有七，家世忠孝。

translations.literal: When Guangdong rebels grew powerful, Yifen saw affairs growing daily more urgent and told others: 'I am seventy-seven years old, and my family has been loyal and filial for generations.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdong rebels grew powerful, Yifen saw affairs growing daily more urgent and told others: 'I am seventy-seven years old, and my family has been loyal and filial for generations.

sentences.zh: 脫有不幸，惟當致命遂志，以見先人。」

translations.literal: If misfortune should come, I can only give my life to fulfill my resolve and show myself worthy before my ancestors.'
translations.idiomatic: If misfortune should come, I can only give my life to fulfill my resolve and show myself worthy before my ancestors.'

sentences.zh: 江寧籌防，大吏每有諮詢，盡言贊畫。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was organizing its defenses, the high officials often consulted him, and he spoke fully in support of their plans.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangning was organizing its defenses, senior officials often consulted him, and he offered his counsel freely.

sentences.zh: 城陷，從容賦絕命詞，赴水死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he calmly composed a final testament and entered the water to die.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he calmly composed a final testament and drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 事聞，文宗以其三世死事，特詔優恤，加一云騎尉，諡貞愍。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Wenzong, because three generations of the family had died in service, issued a special edict of generous condolence, added one Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, and conferred the posthumous title Zhenmin.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Emperor Wenzong, noting that three generations of the family had died in service, issued a special edict of generous mourning honors, added one Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, and gave him the posthumous title Zhenmin, 'Steadfast and Compassionate.'

sentences.zh: 張芾，字小浦，陝西涇陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Fei, styled Xiaopu, was a native of Jingyang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei, styled Xiaopu, was from Jingyang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the fifteenth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷庶子，直南書房。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to tutor of the heir apparent and served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to tutor of the heir apparent and served in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 大考一等，擢少詹事，超遷內閣學士，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: In the triennial examination he ranked first class, was promoted to junior tutor of the heir apparent, was exceptionally promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and supervised education in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the triennial examination he placed first class, was promoted to junior tutor of the heir apparent, was promoted ahead of schedule to grand secretary, and served as educational commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，授工部侍郎，任滿回京，仍直南書房，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed vice minister of Works; when his term ended he returned to the capital, continued service in the Southern Study, and was transferred to the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed vice minister of Works. When his term ended he returned to the capital, continued service in the Southern Study, and was transferred to the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，督江西學政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he supervised education in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he served as educational commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，應詔陳言，請明黜陟，寬出納，禁糜費，重海防，上嘉納。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne, in response to an edict he submitted advice requesting clear promotion and dismissal, lenient revenue collection and disbursement, prohibition of wasteful expenditure, and emphasis on coastal defense; the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, he responded to the imperial call for memorials by urging clear standards for promotion and dismissal, easier revenue collection and disbursement, an end to wasteful spending, and stronger coastal defense; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 命按巡撫陳阡被劾各款，得實，罷之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to investigate the various charges against Governor Chen Qian; they were found true, and Chen was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to investigate the charges against Governor Chen Qian; they were found true, and Chen was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 阡亦訐芾收受陋規，詔免議。

translations.literal: Chen Qian also accused Fei of accepting improper fees; an edict exempted Fei from investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qian also accused Fei of accepting improper fees, but an edict exempted Fei from investigation.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，調刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he was transferred to vice minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he was transferred to vice minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 任滿，留署江西巡撫，尋實授。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was retained to act as governor of Jiangxi, and soon afterward received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was retained as acting governor of Jiangxi, and soon afterward received formal appointment.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪方圍長沙，詔芾偕在籍尚書陳孚恩籌防。

translations.literal: At the time Guangdong rebels were besieging Changsha; an edict ordered Fei to join the retired minister Chen Fu'en in organizing defenses.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Guangdong rebels were besieging Changsha. An edict ordered Fei to join the retired minister Chen Fu'en in organizing defenses.

sentences.zh: 未幾，岳州陷，芾駐守九江。

translations.literal: Before long Yuezhou fell, and Fei stationed himself to defend Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuezhou fell, and Fei took up position at Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，總督陸建瀛至九江，芾移守瑞昌，賊來犯，擊走之，而九江遂陷，革職留任，退守南昌。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Governor-General Lu Jianying arrived at Jiujiang; Fei moved to defend Ruichang, the rebels came to attack and were driven off, but Jiujiang then fell; Fei was stripped of office but kept on duty and withdrew to defend Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Governor-General Lu Jianying arrived at Jiujiang. Fei moved to defend Ruichang, beat back a rebel attack, but Jiujiang then fell. Fei was dismissed from office but kept on duty and fell back to Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 賊既踞江寧，分股溯江而上。

translations.literal: After the rebels had seized Jiangning, detachments moved up the river.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels seized Jiangning, detachments moved upriver.

sentences.zh: 芾奏調湖北按察使江忠源來援，甫至而賊船直抵城下，芾率官紳嬰城固守，賊穴道轟城，壞而復完。

translations.literal: Fei memorialized to transfer Hubei provincial judge Jiang Zhongyuan to aid him; Jiang had just arrived when rebel boats reached the foot of the city wall. Fei led officials and gentry in binding themselves to the city and holding firm; the rebels tunneled and blasted the wall, but it was damaged and then repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Fei memorialized to bring Hubei provincial judge Jiang Zhongyuan to his aid. Jiang had just arrived when rebel boats reached the city walls. Fei led officials and gentry in a desperate defense; the rebels tunneled under the wall and blasted it, but the breach was repaired.

sentences.zh: 總兵馬濟美戰歿城外，賴江忠源迭戰卻賊，被圍凡三閱月，賊乃東走，由九江趨安徽。

translations.literal: Brigade commander Ma Jimei died in battle outside the walls; relying on Jiang Zhongyuan's repeated battles to repel the rebels, the city was besieged for three full months before the rebels finally fled eastward through Jiujiang toward Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade commander Ma Jimei was killed fighting outside the walls. Thanks to Jiang Zhongyuan's repeated victories, the city held through a three-month siege before the rebels finally fled east through Jiujiang toward Anhui.

sentences.zh: 芾以守城勞，復原官。

translations.literal: For his labors in defending the city, Fei was restored to his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in defending the city, Fei was restored to his original rank.

sentences.zh: 奏將將吏猥多，部議覈減，芾疏爭，嚴旨切責。

translations.literal: In his memorial the number of generals and officials recommended for reward was excessively large; the board proposed reduction after review, Fei memorialized in protest, and a stern edict sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial recommended an excessively large number of generals and officials for reward. The board proposed cuts after review, Fei protested in a memorial, and a stern edict sharply rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 會因截留滇、黔銅鉛銀，又陳孚恩被劾，芾為申辨，上怒，褫芾職。

translations.literal: At the same time, because he had intercepted copper, lead, and silver from Yunnan and Guizhou, and because Chen Fu'en had been impeached and Fei spoke in his defense, the emperor grew angry and stripped Fei of office.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, because he had intercepted copper, lead, and silver shipments from Yunnan and Guizhou, and because Chen Fu'en had been impeached and Fei spoke in his defense, the emperor grew angry and stripped Fei of office.

sentences.zh: 芾既罷，道梗不得歸，僑居紹興。

translations.literal: After Fei was dismissed, the roads were blocked and he could not return home, so he lived as a sojourner in Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: After Fei was dismissed, the roads were blocked and he could not return home, so he lived in Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 賊窺徽、寧急，巡撫駐廬州不能兼顧。

translations.literal: The rebels watched for an opening in Huizhou and Ningguo, while the governor, stationed at Luzhou, could not attend to both regions.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels watched for an opening in Huizhou and Ningguo, while the governor, posted at Luzhou, could not cover both regions.

sentences.zh: 侍郎王茂廕薦芾，乃命交和春、福濟差遣。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Wang Maoyin recommended Fei, and he was ordered placed under the command of He Chun and Fu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wang Maoyin recommended Fei, and he was placed under the command of He Chun and Fu Ji.

sentences.zh: 芾至，練團勸捐，以千人守徽州，提督鄧紹良、總兵江長貴分扼要隘。

translations.literal: When Fei arrived, he organized militia and encouraged contributions, kept a thousand men to defend Huizhou, and had regional commander Deng Shaoliang and brigade commander Jiang Changgui hold key passes separately.
translations.idiomatic: When Fei arrived, he organized militia and encouraged contributions, posted a thousand men to defend Huizhou, and had regional commander Deng Shaoliang and brigade commander Jiang Changgui hold key passes.

sentences.zh: 五年，复休寧、石埭，予六品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he recovered Xiuning and Shidi and was granted the sixth-rank official's cap button.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he recovered Xiuning and Shidi and was granted the sixth-rank official's cap button.

sentences.zh: 六年，賊擾婺源、祁門，連破之於七里橋、屯溪口，徽境得安，加五品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the rebels harassed Wuyuan and Qimen; he defeated them in succession at Qili Bridge and Tunxi Pass, the Huizhou region was secured, and he was granted the fifth-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the rebels raided Wuyuan and Qimen; he defeated them in succession at Qili Bridge and Tunxi Pass, secured the Huizhou region, and was granted the fifth-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，賊復由江西竄踞休寧，擊走之。

translations.literal: That winter the rebels again fled from Jiangxi and seized Xiuning; he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the rebels again broke in from Jiangxi and seized Xiuning; he drove them off.

sentences.zh: 母喪，奪情留軍，命俟服闋後以三品京堂候補。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he was granted leave from mourning to remain with the army and was ordered that after mourning ended he would await appointment as third-rank metropolitan official.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he was granted leave from mourning to remain with the army and was told that after mourning he would await appointment as third-rank metropolitan official.

sentences.zh: 七年，鄧紹良戰歿灣沚，祁門、婺源皆告急。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Deng Shaoliang died in battle at Wanzhi, and both Qimen and Wuyuan sent urgent appeals.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Deng Shaoliang was killed in battle at Wanzhi, and both Qimen and Wuyuan sent urgent appeals for help.

sentences.zh: 遣參將王慶麟破賊於清華街，又擊走祁門賊。

translations.literal: He dispatched regimental commander Wang Qinglin, who defeated the rebels at Qinghua Street and also drove off the rebels at Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched regimental commander Wang Qinglin, who defeated the rebels at Qinghua Street and also drove off the rebels at Qimen.

sentences.zh: 九年，复婺源，賊西竄，授芾通政使，尋遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he recovered Wuyuan; the rebels fled westward; Fei was appointed transmission commissioner and soon afterward transferred to vice censor-in-chief of the left.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he recovered Wuyuan and the rebels fled west. Fei was appointed transmission commissioner and soon promoted to vice censor-in-chief of the left.

sentences.zh: 太平、石埭連戰皆捷，詔皖南四府一州軍務歸芾督辦。

translations.literal: Victories followed in successive battles at Taiping and Shidi; an edict placed military affairs of the four prefectures and one department of southern Anhui under Fei's supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Victories followed in successive battles at Taiping and Shidi. An edict placed military affairs of the four prefectures and one department of southern Anhui under Fei's supervision.

sentences.zh: 十年，賊复陷涇縣、旌德，由績溪進犯徽郡。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the rebels again seized Jing County and Jingde and advanced through Jixi to attack Huizhou prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the rebels again took Jing County and Jingde and advanced through Jixi to attack Huizhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 芾督江長貴及知府蘇式敬、道員蕭翰慶，連克太平、旌德、石埭、涇縣，而賊由江蘇、浙江回竄，复連陷建平、廣德、涇縣。

translations.literal: Fei directed Jiang Changgui, prefect Su Shijing, and circuit intendant Xiao Hanqing in recovering Taiping, Jingde, Shidi, and Jing County in succession, but the rebels returned from Jiangsu and Zhejiang and again seized Jianping, Guangde, and Jing County in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Fei directed Jiang Changgui, Prefect Su Shijing, and Circuit Intendant Xiao Hanqing in recovering Taiping, Jingde, Shidi, and Jing County in succession, but the rebels returned from Jiangsu and Zhejiang and again took Jianping, Guangde, and Jing County.

sentences.zh: 芾先以失機自劾，暫行革職留軍，至是復自請治罪，遂命以皖南軍事畀兩江總督曾國籓，召芾還京，請回籍補持服，允之。

translations.literal: Fei had earlier impeached himself for missing his opportunity and was temporarily stripped of office but kept with the army; now he again requested punishment, and the order was given to entrust southern Anhui military affairs to Governor-General Zeng Guofan of the Two Jiangs, recall Fei to the capital, and grant his request to return home to complete mourning; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Fei had earlier impeached himself for missing his chance and was temporarily dismissed but kept with the army. Now he again asked to be punished, and the court entrusted southern Anhui military affairs to Governor-General Zeng Guofan, recalled Fei to the capital, and granted his request to return home to complete mourning.

sentences.zh: 十一年，粵匪、捻匪合擾關中，起芾助治團練禦賊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Guangdong rebels and Nian bandits together harassed Guanzhong; Fei was recalled to help organize militia to resist the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Guangdong rebels and Nian bandits together harassed Guanzhong, and Fei was recalled to help organize militia against them.

sentences.zh: 事甫平，而回匪亂作，連破數州縣，逼省城，詔芾督辦陝西團練，會同巡撫瑛棨防剿。

translations.literal: Affairs had just settled when a Hui rebellion broke out, several prefectures and counties were taken in succession, and the provincial capital was threatened; an edict ordered Fei to supervise Shaanxi militia and join Governor Ying Qi in defense and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs had barely settled when a Hui rebellion broke out, several prefectures and counties fell in succession, and the provincial capital was threatened. An edict ordered Fei to supervise Shaanxi militia and join Governor Ying Qi in defense and suppression.

sentences.zh: 瑛棨巽懦，計無所出，謂芾大臣有鄉望，諭之宜可解。

translations.literal: Ying Qi was timid and irresolute and could think of no plan; he said Fei was a senior official with local prestige and urged that he ought to be able to resolve the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Qi was timid and irresolute and could think of no plan. He said Fei was a senior official with local prestige and urged that he ought to be able to resolve the matter.

sentences.zh: 芾慨然率數騎往，歷高陵、臨潼至渭南倉頭鎮，曉以利害，回眾頗感動。

translations.literal: Fei resolutely led a few horsemen there, passing through Gaoling and Lintong to Cangtou Town in Weinan, where he explained the advantages and disadvantages; the Hui crowd was considerably moved.
translations.idiomatic: Fei resolutely led a few horsemen there, passing through Gaoling and Lintong to Cangtou Town in Weinan, where he explained the stakes; the Hui crowd was considerably moved.

sentences.zh: 其酋任老五懼搖眾心，嗾黨擁出折辱之，芾據地大罵不絕口，遂被支解。

translations.literal: Their chieftain Ren Laowu, fearing that hearts would be swayed, incited his followers to rush out and humiliate him; Fei sat on the ground cursing without cease and was dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftain Ren Laowu, fearing the crowd would be swayed, incited his followers to rush out and humiliate him. Fei sat on the ground cursing without pause and was hacked to pieces.

sentences.zh: 時同治元年五月十三日也。

translations.literal: This was on the thirteenth day of the fifth month of the first year of Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: This was on the thirteenth day of the fifth month of the first year of Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: 子師劬，往覓遺骸，僅得骨數節。

translations.literal: His son Shiju went to search for the remains and recovered only a few fragments of bone.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiju went to search for the remains and recovered only a few fragments of bone.

sentences.zh: 事聞，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡文毅。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was granted the combined hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, and the posthumous title Wenyi was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was granted the combined hereditary ranks of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Cloud Cavalry and given the posthumous title Wenyi, 'Cultured Resolve.'

sentences.zh: 命於省城、倉頭鎮並建專祠，隨行遇害之臨潼知縣繆樹本、山西知縣蔣若訥及家屬在涇陽被害者五十二人，從死僕人金榜等六人，並附祀。

translations.literal: Orders were given to build special shrines both in the provincial capital and at Cangtou Town; Lintong magistrate Miu Shuben and Shanxi magistrate Jiang Ruone, who were killed on the journey, fifty-two family members killed at Jingyang, and six servants who died with them, including Jin Bang, were all enshrined there as well.
translations.idiomatic: Orders were given to build special shrines in both the provincial capital and Cangtou Town. Lintong magistrate Miu Shuben and Shanxi magistrate Jiang Ruone, who were killed on the journey, fifty-two family members killed at Jingyang, and six servants who died with them, including Jin Bang, were all enshrined there as well.

sentences.zh: 賜師劬舉人。

translations.literal: Shiju was granted the status of provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Shiju was granted the status of provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 江西、徽州並建專祠，後祀江西名宦。

translations.literal: Special shrines were also built in Jiangxi and Huizhou, and later he was enshrined in the Hall of Eminent Officials of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Special shrines were also built in Jiangxi and Huizhou, and later he was enshrined in Jiangxi's Hall of Eminent Officials.

sentences.zh: 黃琮，雲南昆明人。

translations.literal: Huang Cong, a native of Kunming in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Cong was from Kunming in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 道光六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the sixth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 累擢兵部侍郎，以親老乞養回籍。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to vice minister of War and, because his parents were elderly, requested leave to care for them and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to vice minister of War and, when his parents grew old, requested leave to care for them and returned home.

sentences.zh: 咸豐七年，雲南迴亂方熾，命琮偕在籍御史竇垿治團練。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xianfeng the Hui rebellion in Yunnan was blazing; Cong was ordered to join the retired censor Dou Kai in organizing militia.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xianfeng the Hui rebellion in Yunnan was at its height. Cong was ordered to join the retired censor Dou Kai in organizing militia.

sentences.zh: 時餉絀兵單，疆臣主且剿且撫，而漢、回仇隙素深，團練驕悍不聽約束，往往撫局將成，練勇擅殺降回，益紛擾。

translations.literal: At the time funds were short and troops few; frontier officials favored both suppression and pacification, but Han-Hui enmity ran deep, the militia were arrogant and fierce and would not obey restraint, and often just as pacification was about to succeed militiamen would on their own kill surrendering Hui, making affairs all the more chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: Funds were short and troops few. Frontier officials favored both suppression and pacification, but Han-Hui enmity ran deep. The militia were arrogant and unruly, and often just as pacification was about to succeed militiamen would kill surrendering Hui on their own, making matters all the more chaotic.

sentences.zh: 總督吳振棫劾琮及竇垿辦理失當，皆褫職。

translations.literal: Governor-General Wu Zhenbang impeached Cong and Dou Kai for mishandling affairs, and both were stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Wu Zhenbang impeached Cong and Dou Kai for mishandling affairs, and both were stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 事稍定，振棫疏陳縱容練勇諸事，皆出竇垿主持。

translations.literal: When affairs had settled somewhat, Zhenbang memorialized that the matters of indulging the militia had all been directed by Dou Kai.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs had settled somewhat, Zhenbang memorialized that the indulgence of the militia had all been directed by Dou Kai.

sentences.zh: 琮當省城被圍時，登陴固守有勞，又勸捐出力，詔復原官。

translations.literal: When the provincial capital was besieged, Cong had labored in mounting the walls to hold firm and had also exerted himself in encouraging contributions; an edict restored his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the provincial capital was besieged, Cong had labored on the walls to hold the city and had also worked hard to encourage contributions. An edict restored his original rank.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，逆回馬榮詐降，入城戕總督潘鐸，肆殺掠，琮遇害，贈右都御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi the rebel Hui Ma Rong feigned surrender, entered the city and killed Governor Pan Duo, slaughtered and plundered freely, and Cong was killed; he was posthumously granted the rank of censor-in-chief of the right.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi the rebel Hui Ma Rong feigned surrender, entered the city and killed Governor Pan Duo, then slaughtered and plundered freely. Cong was killed and was posthumously granted the rank of censor-in-chief of the right.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，巡撫潘鼎新為請，予諡文潔。

translations.literal: During the Guangxu reign Governor Pan Dingxin requested honors on his behalf, and the posthumous title Wenjie was granted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu reign Governor Pan Dingxin requested honors on his behalf, and he was given the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Cultured Purity.'

sentences.zh: 陶廷傑，貴州都勻人。

translations.literal: Tao Tingjie, a native of Duyun in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Tingjie was from Duyun in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年進士，由編修遷御史、給事中。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the metropolitan examination, rose from compiler to censor and supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the nineteenth year of Jiaqing and rose from compiler to censor and supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 道光中，出為江蘇蘇松糧儲道。

translations.literal: During the Daoguang reign he went out to serve as grain transport commissioner of Su-Song in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daoguang reign he served as grain transport commissioner of Su-Song in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 歷甘肅按察使、陝西布政使，署巡撫。

translations.literal: He served successively as provincial judge of Gansu and provincial treasurer of Shaanxi and acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as provincial judge of Gansu and provincial treasurer of Shaanxi and acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，休致。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he retired.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，貴州土匪起，命廷傑在籍會同地方官辦理團練。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng bandits rose in Guizhou; Tingjie was ordered, while at home, to join local officials in organizing militia.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng bandits rose in Guizhou. Tingjie was ordered, while at home, to join local officials in organizing militia.

sentences.zh: 六年，古州、黃平、都勻先後陷，廷傑率團練禦賊，死之，予騎都尉世職，諡文節。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Guzhou, Huangping, and Duyun fell in succession; Tingjie led militia to resist the rebels and died; he was granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry and the posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Guzhou, Huangping, and Duyun fell in succession. Tingjie led militia against the rebels and died. He was granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry and the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Cultured Integrity.'

sentences.zh: 馮培元，字因伯，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: Feng Peiyuan, styled Yinbo, was a native of Renhe in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Peiyuan, styled Yinbo, was from Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光二十四年一甲三名進士，授編修，入直南書房。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination as third in the first class, was appointed compiler, and entered attendance in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang he placed third in the first class of metropolitan graduates, was appointed a compiler, and entered service in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，改直上書房，授惇郡王奕脤讀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was transferred to attendance in the Upper Study and instructed the Prince of Dun, Yicong, in reading.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he was transferred to the Upper Study and tutored the Prince of Dun, Yicong.

sentences.zh: 二年，大考二等，擢侍講。

translations.literal: In the second year, in the triennial examination he ranked second class and was promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he placed second class in the triennial examination and was promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 尋督湖北學政。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he supervised education in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served as educational commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 數月中，連擢侍講學士、光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: Within a few months he was promoted in succession to reader of the Hanlin Academy and director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was promoted in succession to Hanlin reader and director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪已犯長沙，人情洶懼。

translations.literal: At the time Guangdong rebels had already attacked Changsha, and public sentiment was alarmed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: By then Guangdong rebels had already struck Changsha, and public panic was spreading.

sentences.zh: 培元幼孤，家貧，母何賢明苦節，撫之成立。

translations.literal: Peiyuan lost his father in youth; his family was poor, and his mother He was wise, virtuous, and steadfast in hardship, raising him to maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Peiyuan was orphaned young and grew up poor. His mother He was wise and steadfast through hardship and raised him to adulthood.

sentences.zh: 及至湖北，將迎養。

translations.literal: When he reached Hubei he was about to bring her to live with him and support her.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Hubei he was about to bring her to live with him and support her in his home.

sentences.zh: 聞岳州陷，馳書止母行。

translations.literal: When he heard that Yuezhou had fallen, he sent an urgent letter stopping his mother from coming.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Yuezhou had fallen, he sent an urgent letter telling his mother not to come.

sentences.zh: 母報曰：「如果有變，見危授命，大節不可奪。

translations.literal: His mother replied: 'If there should be a crisis, meet danger and give your life; great integrity must not be compromised.
translations.idiomatic: His mother replied: 'If crisis comes, meet danger and give your life. Great integrity must never be compromised.

sentences.zh: 其遵吾教！」

translations.literal: Obey my teaching!'
translations.idiomatic: Obey what I have taught you!'

sentences.zh: 培元奉書，涕泣自矢。

translations.literal: Peiyuan received the letter, wept, and pledged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Peiyuan received the letter, wept, and pledged himself to her charge.

sentences.zh: 賊至攻城，培元偕在城文武登陴同守。

translations.literal: When the rebels arrived and attacked the city, Peiyuan joined the civil and military officials in the city in mounting the walls to defend together.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived and attacked the city, Peiyuan joined the civil and military officials inside in mounting the walls to defend it.

sentences.zh: 城陷，投井死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he threw himself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，賊去，向榮率兵入城，有以告者，始出而殮之，屍如生。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year the rebels departed; Xiang Rong led troops into the city, and when someone reported the matter his body was at last recovered and encoffined, looking as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year the rebels withdrew. Xiang Rong led troops into the city, and when someone reported what had happened, the body was at last recovered and encoffined, looking as if he were still alive.

sentences.zh: 事聞，文宗以武昌之陷，闔城文武殉難，卹典特優，贈侍郎，建專祠，予騎都尉世職，諡文介。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Wenzong, because of the fall of Wuchang and the martyrdom of the entire city's civil and military officials, granted especially generous condolence honors, posthumously appointed him vice minister, built a special shrine, granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and conferred the posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Emperor Wenzong, noting that with the fall of Wuchang the city's entire civil and military corps had died in service, granted especially generous mourning honors, posthumously made him vice minister, ordered a special shrine built, granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and gave him the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Cultured Integrity.'

sentences.zh: 後兩子學瀚、學澧皆賜舉人。

translations.literal: Later both his sons Xuehan and Xueli were granted the status of provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Later both his sons Xuehan and Xueli were granted the status of provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 孫銘恩，字蘭檢，江蘇通州人。

translations.literal: Sun Mingen, styled Lanjian, was a native of Tongzhou in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mingen, styled Lanjian, was from Tongzhou in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，累遷詹事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiler, and was promoted step by step to tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the fifteenth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was appointed a compiler, and rose step by step to tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，典試廣東，還京，道出九江。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he served as chief examiner in Guangdong; returning to the capital, his route passed through Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he served as chief examiner in Guangdong. On his return to the capital his route passed through Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 粵匪已由岳州東下，陷漢陽。

translations.literal: Guangdong rebels had already moved east from Yuezhou and taken Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong rebels had already moved east from Yuezhou and taken Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 銘恩疏上江防十二事，下江南督撫施行。
