translations.literal: Mingen memorialized twelve measures for river defense, which were transmitted to the governors of Jiangnan for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Mingen memorialized twelve measures for river defense, which were sent down to the Jiangnan governors for implementation.

sentences.zh: 三年，連擢內閣學士、兵部侍郎，督安徽學政。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted in succession to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat and vice minister of War, and supervised education in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted in succession to grand secretary and vice minister of War, and served as educational commissioner of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 時安慶已為賊踞，故事，學政駐太平府，銘恩激勵紳民，舉行團練，捐廉為倡。

translations.literal: At the time Anqing was already held by rebels; by precedent the educational commissioner resided at Taiping Prefecture. Mingen encouraged gentry and people, organized militia, and took the lead by donating from his official salary.
translations.idiomatic: Anqing was already in rebel hands. By precedent the educational commissioner resided at Taiping Prefecture. Mingen rallied gentry and commoners, organized militia, and led by donating from his own salary.

sentences.zh: 潰兵時至，侮官劫市，銘恩諭以大義，稍定。

translations.literal: Routed troops arrived from time to time, insulting officials and plundering the markets; Mingen admonished them with the larger moral duty, and matters settled somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Routed troops kept arriving, insulting officials and plundering the markets. Mingen admonished them with appeals to duty, and the disorder eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 四年，以父病請開缺省視，會有旨命偕在籍前南河總督潘錫恩防守徽、寧，銘恩未之知也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, because his father was ill he requested leave from office to return and care for him; at the same time an edict ordered him to join the retired former governor-general of the South River, Pan Xien, in defending Huizhou and Ningguo, but Mingen did not yet know of this.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when his father fell ill, he asked leave from office to return home and care for him. At the same time an edict ordered him to join the retired former governor-general of the South River, Pan Xien, in defending Huizhou and Ningguo, but Mingen did not yet know of it.

sentences.zh: 疏入，文宗疑其規避，嚴旨切責，允其回籍，俟假滿以三四品京堂降補。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Wenzong suspected he was evading duty and issued a stern edict sharply rebuking him; he was permitted to return home and, after leave ended, to await appointment as a third- or fourth-rank metropolitan official at reduced rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Emperor Wenzong suspected he was evading duty and issued a stern rebuke. He was allowed to return home and, after leave ended, to await appointment as a third- or fourth-rank metropolitan official at reduced rank.

sentences.zh: 未踰月，賊犯太平，從者請避之。

translations.literal: Before a month had passed the rebels attacked Taiping, and his attendants asked him to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Before a month had passed the rebels attacked Taiping, and his attendants urged him to flee.

sentences.zh: 銘恩曰：「城亡與亡，以明吾心！」

translations.literal: Mingen said: 'If the city falls, I fall with it, to show where my heart stands!'
translations.idiomatic: Mingen said: 'If the city falls, I fall with it—that is how I show where my heart stands!'

sentences.zh: 城陷，賊至，衣冠坐堂上，抗罵，被執，囚於江寧，僕范源從。

translations.literal: When the city fell and the rebels arrived, he sat in official dress in the hall, cursed them defiantly, was seized, imprisoned in Jiangning, and his servant Fan Yuan followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell and the rebels arrived, he sat in official dress in the hall and cursed them defiantly. He was seized and imprisoned in Jiangning, and his servant Fan Yuan followed him.

sentences.zh: 銘恩不食，賊脅源勸降，源叱之，斷其舌，同遇害。

translations.literal: Mingen refused to eat; the rebels forced Yuan to urge surrender, Yuan rebuked them, his tongue was cut out, and both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Mingen refused to eat. The rebels forced Yuan to urge him to surrender; Yuan rebuked them, had his tongue cut out, and both were killed.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其抗節不屈，遇害甚慘，贈內閣學士，入祀京師及安徽、江蘇昭忠祠，予騎都尉世職，諡文節。

translations.literal: An edict praised his unyielding integrity and the terrible cruelty of his death, posthumously appointed him grand secretary, enshrined him in the Hall of Loyalty and Devotion in the capital and in Anhui and Jiangsu, granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and conferred the posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised his unyielding integrity and the terrible cruelty of his death, posthumously made him grand secretary, enshrined him in the Hall of Loyalty and Devotion in the capital and in Anhui and Jiangsu, granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and gave him the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Cultured Integrity.'

sentences.zh: 范源同議卹。

translations.literal: Fan Yuan was granted condolence honors as well.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yuan was granted mourning honors as well.

sentences.zh: 沈炳垣，字紫卿，浙江海鹽人。

translations.literal: Shen Bingyuan, styled Ziqing, was a native of Haiyan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Bingyuan, styled Ziqing, was from Haiyan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光二十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷中允。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiler, and was transferred to assistant director of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was appointed a compiler, and was transferred to assistant director of the Academy.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，督廣西學政。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he supervised education in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he served as educational commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 廣西自洪秀全北犯後，群匪迭起。

translations.literal: After Hong Xiuquan marched north from Guangxi, bandit groups rose one after another.
translations.idiomatic: After Hong Xiuquan marched north from Guangxi, bandit groups rose one after another.

sentences.zh: 炳垣至，與巡撫勞崇光議戰守策，崇光深器之。

translations.literal: When Bingyuan arrived he discussed plans for war and defense with Governor Lao Chongguang, who greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingyuan arrived he discussed plans for war and defense with Governor Lao Chongguang, who greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 七年春，按試南寧畢，警報日至，居民洶洶驚避。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, when examinations in Nanning were finished, alarms arrived daily and the residents were alarmed and fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year, when examinations in Nanning were finished, alarms arrived daily and residents fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 炳垣倡言城險可保，條列守禦法，捐俸濟餉，守三晝夜。

translations.literal: Bingyuan declared that the city's terrain made it defensible, set forth methods of defense in detail, donated his salary to support the troops, and held for three days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Bingyuan declared that the city's terrain made it defensible, laid out detailed plans for defense, donated his salary to support the troops, and held the city for three days and nights.

sentences.zh: 賊知有備，引去。

translations.literal: The rebels, seeing preparations in place, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the city prepared, the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 潯州陷，江路梗塞，間道至梧州。

translations.literal: When Xunzhou fell the river route was blocked, and he reached Wuzhou by a side path.
translations.idiomatic: When Xunzhou fell the river route was blocked, and he reached Wuzhou by a side path.

sentences.zh: 艇匪陳開等眾數万突來犯，炳垣率知府陳瑞枝等嬰城固守，凡三閱月，糧盡援絕。

translations.literal: Boat bandits led by Chen Kai and others, numbering tens of thousands, suddenly attacked; Bingyuan led Prefect Chen Ruizhi and others in binding themselves to the city and holding firm for three full months until grain was exhausted and relief cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Boat bandits led by Chen Kai and others, numbering tens of thousands, suddenly attacked. Bingyuan led Prefect Chen Ruizhi and others in a desperate defense of the city for three full months until grain ran out and relief was cut off.

sentences.zh: 官吏以炳垣無守土責，遣兵衛之出，炳垣不可。

translations.literal: Officials, saying Bingyuan bore no territorial defense duty, sent troops to escort him out, but he would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, saying Bingyuan had no duty to hold territory, sent troops to escort him out, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 八月，城陷，仰藥未死，賊擁去，厚遇之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the city fell; he swallowed poison but did not die, was seized by the rebels and taken away, and was treated with great consideration.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the city fell. He swallowed poison but did not die, was seized by the rebels, and was treated with surprising consideration.

sentences.zh: 炳垣罵賊，求死不得。

translations.literal: Bingyuan cursed the rebels and could not obtain death.
translations.idiomatic: Bingyuan cursed the rebels but could not obtain death.

sentences.zh: 久之，乘間為書致巡撫劉長佑，請出兵襲城，密約城內民夾擊。

translations.literal: After a long time he seized an opportunity to write to Governor Liu Changyou, requesting that troops be sent to strike the city and secretly arranging with people inside for a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he seized an opportunity to write to Governor Liu Changyou, asking that troops be sent to strike the city and secretly arranging with people inside for a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 事泄，賊恨甚，磔而焚之。

translations.literal: When the plot leaked out the rebels hated him intensely, dismembered him, and burned his body.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot leaked out the rebels hated him intensely, dismembered him, and burned his body.

sentences.zh: 有老卒睹炳垣慘死狀，走省城首於官。

translations.literal: An old soldier who witnessed Bingyuan's horrific death ran to the provincial capital and reported it first to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: An old soldier who witnessed Bingyuan's horrific death ran to the provincial capital and reported it to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 贈內閣學士，諡文節，建專祠桂林。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed grand secretary, granted the posthumous title Wenjie, and a special shrine was built for him in Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand secretary, given the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Cultured Integrity,' and a special shrine was built for him in Guilin.

sentences.zh: 張錫庚，字星白，江蘇丹徒人，大學士玉書裔孫。

translations.literal: Zhang Xigeng, styled Xingbai, was a native of Dantu in Jiangsu and a descendant of Grand Secretary Yushu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xigeng, styled Xingbai, was from Dantu in Jiangsu and a descendant of Grand Secretary Yushu.

sentences.zh: 道光十六年二甲一名進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination as first in the second class, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the sixteenth year of Daoguang as first in the second class, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷御史，擢順天府丞，丁父憂，服闋，補原官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor, promoted to vice prefect of Shuntian, entered mourning for his father, and when mourning ended resumed his original post.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to censor, was promoted to vice prefect of Shuntian, mourned his father, and when mourning ended resumed his original post.

sentences.zh: 疏論綠營冒濫頂名及緝捕諸弊，詔下其疏於各直省，實力整頓。

translations.literal: He memorialized on abuses in the Green Standard Army such as fraudulent names on the rolls and failures in pursuit and capture; an edict transmitted his memorial to all provinces for earnest rectification.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on abuses in the Green Standard Army such as fraudulent names on the rolls and failures in pursuit and capture. An edict sent his memorial to all provinces for earnest rectification.

sentences.zh: 又疏言殿試貢士不限字數，聽其發抒，刪去頌辭，下部議行。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that palace examination candidates should not be limited in length, should be allowed free expression, and that eulogistic formulae should be removed; the boards were ordered to deliberate and implement this.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that palace examination candidates should not be limited in length, should be allowed free expression, and that eulogistic formulae should be removed. The boards were ordered to deliberate and implement this.

sentences.zh: 歷太僕寺卿、左副都御史。

translations.literal: He served successively as director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and vice censor-in-chief of the left.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and vice censor-in-chief of the left.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，督浙江學政，擢刑部侍郎，仍留學政任。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng he supervised education in Zhejiang, was promoted to vice minister of Punishments, and remained in his post as educational commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xianfeng he served as educational commissioner of Zhejiang, was promoted to vice minister of Punishments, and remained in his educational post.

sentences.zh: 十年，杭州陷而旋复，錫庚助城守，其子恩然率家屬自焚，錫庚以聞，予旌卹。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Hangzhou fell and was soon recovered; Xigeng helped defend the city, his son Enran led the family in self-immolation, Xigeng reported this, and commendation and condolence honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Hangzhou fell and was soon recovered. Xigeng helped defend the city; his son Enran led the family in self-immolation. Xigeng reported this, and commendation and mourning honors were granted.

sentences.zh: 團練大臣王履謙劾巡撫王有齡籌餉按缺派捐，命錫庚訪按。

translations.literal: Militia commissioner Wang Luqian impeached Governor Wang Youling for raising funds by assigning contributions according to vacancies; Xigeng was ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Militia commissioner Wang Luqian impeached Governor Wang Youling for raising funds by assigning contributions according to vacancies. Xigeng was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 錫庚以有齡一月內更易州縣二十馀員，非政體，請予處分，從之。

translations.literal: Xigeng reported that within one month Youling had replaced more than twenty prefects and magistrates, which was not proper administrative practice, and requested punishment; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Xigeng reported that within one month Youling had replaced more than twenty prefects and magistrates, which was not proper administrative practice, and requested punishment. The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 十一年，任滿，代者未至，杭州復被圍，錫庚同守城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year his term ended but his replacement had not arrived; Hangzhou was besieged again, and Xigeng joined in defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year his term ended but his replacement had not arrived. Hangzhou was besieged again, and Xigeng joined in defending the city.

sentences.zh: 城陷，或勸之去，錫庚曰：「吾大臣也，不可辱國！」

translations.literal: When the city fell some urged him to flee; Xigeng said: 'I am a senior minister; I cannot disgrace the state!'
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell some urged him to flee. Xigeng said: 'I am a senior minister. I cannot disgrace the state!'

sentences.zh: 遂自縊，賊稱其忠，為具棺斂。

translations.literal: He then hanged himself; the rebels praised his loyalty and provided a coffin and burial.
translations.idiomatic: He then hanged himself. The rebels praised his loyalty and provided a coffin and burial.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書銜，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，祀浙江昭忠祠，諡文貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted ministerial rank, given the combined hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, enshrined in the Hall of Loyalty and Devotion of Zhejiang, and conferred the posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted ministerial rank, given the combined hereditary ranks of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, enshrined in Zhejiang's Hall of Loyalty and Devotion, and given the posthumous title Wenzhen, 'Cultured Fidelity.'

sentences.zh: 論曰：呂賢基以忠鯁受主知，其治兵安徽也，志欲大有所為，當殘破之馀，驟無藉手，倉猝殞身，文宗惜之。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Lü Xianji won the ruler's trust through loyal forthrightness; when he took command of troops in Anhui he aspired to achieve great things, but amid the ruins of devastation he suddenly had nothing to work with and perished in haste, and Wenzong mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Lü Xianji won the emperor's trust through loyal forthrightness. When he took command in Anhui he aspired to achieve great things, but amid the ruins of devastation he suddenly had nothing to work with and died in haste. Emperor Wenzong mourned him.

sentences.zh: 鄒鳴鶴久著循聲，戴熙亦負清望，張芾守江西、防皖南，雖無偉績，備歷艱難。

translations.literal: Zou Minghe long enjoyed a reputation for good governance, Dai Xi also bore a reputation for integrity, and Zhang Fei defended Jiangxi and guarded southern Anhui; though they achieved no great feats, all endured great hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Minghe long enjoyed a reputation for good governance, Dai Xi also bore a reputation for integrity, and Zhang Fei defended Jiangxi and guarded southern Anhui. Though they achieved no great feats, all endured great hardship.

sentences.zh: 三人以在籍搢紳治團籌防，雖久暫不同，皆事權不屬，或以城亡與亡，或以犯難遇害。

translations.literal: Three of them, as local gentry at home organizing militia and planning defense, though differing in duration, all lacked proper command authority; some died when their cities fell, others were killed in the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Three of them, as local gentry at home organizing militia and planning defense, differed in how long they served and lacked proper command authority; some died when their cities fell, others were killed in the crisis.

sentences.zh: 黃琮初因措置失宜獲咎，繼亦原之，而終不免於難。

translations.literal: Huang Cong was first punished for improper arrangements, later pardoned, but in the end could not escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Cong was first punished for mishandling affairs, later pardoned, but in the end could not escape disaster.

sentences.zh: 馮培元、孫銘恩、沈炳垣、張錫庚，文學之臣，職非守土，死皆慘烈，朝廷報忠之典悉從優渥，固不以成敗論已。

translations.literal: Feng Peiyuan, Sun Mingen, Shen Bingyuan, and Zhang Xigeng were literary officials whose duties did not include territorial defense; all died in terrible circumstances, yet the court's rewards for loyalty were altogether generous, for merit in loyalty is not judged by success or failure alone.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Peiyuan, Sun Mingen, Shen Bingyuan, and Zhang Xigeng were literary officials whose duties did not include holding territory; all died in terrible circumstances, yet the court's rewards for loyalty were altogether generous, for loyalty is not judged by success or failure alone.
